title: improve-quant-kernels-int8-fp8-smoothquant-dequant-fusion-kvcache-batching
author: Aisha Malik
description: Motivation: reduce token cost and tail latency for quantized inference paths (INT8/FP8) by fusing dequantization into matmul kernels, integrating SmoothQuant scaling into the kernel pipeline, and improving scheduling + KV cache behavior for continuous batching workloads. Approach: 1) Add fused dequant+gemm kernels for INT8 and FP8 representations with per-channel scaling support; 2) integrate SmoothQuant scale factors into kernel prologue so we avoid separate pre-scaling passes; 3) implement dequant fusion path that bypasses an intermediate full-precision buffer and performs accumulation in FP32/FP16 as appropriate; 4) scheduler changes: stripe-based continuous batching that groups requests by sequence length quantiles to reduce padded compute; 5) KV cache improvements: pinned GPU pages for hot KV ranges and async prefetch for next-token decode to reduce stalls. This PR includes microbench harness results demonstrating 1.6-2.4x throughput improvement on INT8 matmuls for typical sequence lengths, 10-25% end-to-end token latency reduction in streaming decode, and 12-30% lower GPU memory traffic for quantized models. Backwards-compat: no API changes. Includes new unit tests and end-to-end benchmarks. See related Linear tasks ENG-4289, ENG-4333.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) add fused quantized kernels and smoothquant integration; 2) add scheduler + kvcache prefetch logic and tests; 3) benchmark numbers, fixing CI test flakes and docs updates
review_comments: Jordan Lee: Can you add a microbenchmark that isolates the dequant+gemm path with realistic scaling factors? The current numbers look promising but we need a reproducible harness.
Aisha Malik: Added bench harness and reproducible runner; results included in third_party/bench and docs. Also added comment blocks explaining fused kernel assumptions.
Priya Natarajan: Please ensure the scheduler change is optional and guarded by config flag so Dedicated customers can opt-in after validation.
Aisha Malik: Added 'enable_stripe_batching' runtime flag and feature gate with default off for Dedicated until we validate auto-scaling implications.
Marcus Chen: One test flaky on CI (test_quant_gemm_fp8) — looks like a nondeterministic ordering in the kernel launch path. Can you fix?
Aisha Malik: Fixed race in kernel launch ordering by moving stream synchronization point; re-ran CI and test passed.
ci_details: CI: linux-build (pass), unit-tests (pass after rerun), bench-ci (pass), clang-tidy (pass), fuzz (pass) — one flaky unit test rerun resolved
benchmarks_summary: On A100-like hardware: INT8 fused kernel shows 1.6-2.4x throughput vs previous dequant-then-gemm baseline across 128-512 seq lengths; FP8 kernels show 1.2-1.8x improvement. End-to-end decode experiments with stride batching show 10-25% latency p95 reductions. KV cache prefetching reduces stalls by ~18% in streaming workloads.
testing_notes: Adds unit tests for fused kernels (test_quant_kernels.py), e2e perf test (quant_perf_test.py) and a deterministic bench harness. CI revealed one ordering race which was fixed. All new tests included in presubmit.
release_notes: Performance: Improved quantized inference throughput and latency for INT8/FP8 via fused dequant+GEMM kernels, SmoothQuant integration, and scheduler + KV cache optimizations. No API changes. Customers may opt into 'enable_stripe_batching' and should see lower token costs for quantized models.
merge_commit_message: squash: fused quant kernels + smoothquant + scheduling + kv-prefetch — improves quantized inference throughput and latency
notes: Follow-ups: 1) run longer Dedicated soak tests with stripe batching under multi-tenant load (ENG-4360); 2) add autotuning to pick INT8 vs FP8 kernel based on dynamic token distribution; 3) upstream a subset of kernels to redwood-model-registry for reuse.
